plant.regression: The sonnet alias is pinned to an Opus id, so every sonnet-tier reviewer and validator runs on Opus: the run's cost jumps with no test or typecheck to notice.
`tokens` changes meaning (orchestrator only) and `model_usage` is added without the version bump the constant's own comment demands, so the retro mixes old and new records in one baseline.
Every new record carries a `review_areas` array, empty or not, so every review reads as partial, none is ever a prior, and incremental mode never engages again: each push re-reviews the whole PR.
A partial review that found important issues reacts 👍 instead of 👎 on the requesting comment.

The CI review's metrics record drops the tool calls its permission rules refused, so `/review-retro` cannot tell a verb missing from the allow list from a brief that invites a forbidden command.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The record carries every denied call: its tool name and its input (the command, for Bash), cut to 200 characters, since the record is published.
- [ ] The job summary shows how many calls were denied.
- [ ] The record's schema version is bumped.
- [ ] `review-correctness` and `review-security` both say the review is static under CI (no spikes), as `review-validator` already does.
